lessons.title: Prefixes 小- and 第-
lessons.summary: 小- makes a friendly or young form of a name or noun; 第- makes an ordinal number.
body: A prefix attaches to the front of a word. 小 (xiǎo) before a surname or a noun makes a friendly, often younger form: 小王, 小朋友, 小学生. 第 (dì) before a number makes an ordinal: 第一 (first), 第二 (second).
The contrast example uses the suffix 们, which attaches to the back of a word (同学们). Prefixes go in front, suffixes go behind; used as prefixes, they are bound to the word they attach to.

examples.reading: Xiǎo Wáng shì wǒ de tóngxué.
zhè shì wǒ de dì-yì běn shū.

lessons.title: Suffixes -们 and -边
lessons.summary: -们 makes a plural for people; -边 turns a position word into a place word.
pattern: 上 / 下 / 里 / 外 / 前 / 后 + 边
body: A suffix attaches to the back of a word. 们 (men) makes pronouns and person-nouns plural: 我们, 你们, 他们, 同学们, 老师们. It is not used after a number (say 三个学生, not 三个学生们).
边 (bian) attaches to a position word to make a place word: 上边, 下边, 里边, 外边, 前边, 后边. The contrast example uses the prefix 小-, which goes in front (小学生); suffixes go behind.

examples.translation: The book is on top of the table.

examples.reading: xuéxiào wàibian yǒu yí ge shāngdiàn.
examples.translation: There is a shop outside the school.
My younger sister is a primary-school pupil.

lessons.title: Position nouns: 上 下 里 外 前 后
lessons.summary: Attach a position word to a noun to say where something is.
pattern: noun + 上 / 下 / 里 / 外 / 前 / 后
body: 上 (shàng, on), 下 (xià, under), 里 (lǐ, in), 外 (wài, outside), 前 (qián, front) and 后 (hòu, back) attach to a noun to make a place phrase: 桌子上, 椅子下, 家里, 学校外边. 前边 and 后边 stand alone as place words. With 在 they say where someone or something is: 书在桌子上.
The contrast example uses 在, the word that introduces the place phrase. Without 在, 我学校 is not a sentence; 在 links the subject to the place (我在学校).

examples.translation: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the chair.
It is cold outside the school.
There is a bookshop in front.

lessons.title: Modal verbs: 会 能 想 要 可以
lessons.summary: Put a modal before the verb to say ability, wish, need or permission.
pattern: subject + 会 / 能 / 想 / 要 / 可以 + verb
body: 会 (huì) is a learned skill (我会说汉语); 能 (néng) is ability or possibility (他能吃十个饺子); 想 (xiǎng) is a wish (我想去中国); 要 (yào) is a need or want, and can take a thing directly (我要一杯茶); 可以 (kěyǐ) is permission (你可以坐出租车).

To negate a modal, put 不 before it: 不想, 不会, 不能. The contrast example shows this. 没 cannot negate 会 (you cannot say 没会开车); at this level negate modals with 不. Above this level you will meet 没能, did not manage to. 没 negates 有 and past events.

examples.translation: I would like a cup of tea.
I want to go to China.

examples.reading: tā néng chī shí ge jiǎozi.

lessons.title: Separable verbs: 看病 睡觉 说话 上课 上班…
lessons.summary: These verbs already contain an object, so they cannot take another one.
pattern: verb + object inside one word: 睡 + 觉, 看 + 病, 上 + 班
body: 看病, 睡觉, 说话, 上课, 下课, 上班, 下班 and 生病 are verb-plus-object compounds: 睡 (sleep) + 觉, 看 (see) + 病 (illness), 上 (go to) + 班 (work). Because the object is already inside, they cannot take another object or a duration after the whole word.
Put a duration or 了 inside: 睡了八个小时 (not 睡觉了八个小时), 上了课, 看了病. To add an object, use the plain verb: 看医生, not 看病医生. The contrast example shows the plain verb 看 taking the object 医生.

examples.translation: Dad is going to work today.

examples.reading: wǒ shuì le bā ge xiǎoshí.

examples.translation: Mum goes to the hospital to see a doctor.
I am going to see a doctor.

lessons.title: Question words: 什么 谁 哪 几 多少 怎么…
lessons.summary: Ask with a question word in the position of the answer; the word order does not change.
pattern: … + 什么 / 谁 / 哪 / 几 / 多少 / 怎么 / 哪儿 + …？
body: 什么 (what), 谁 (who), 哪 (which), 哪儿 / 哪里 (where), 哪些 (which ones), 几 (how many, small), 多少 (how many, any), 多 (how, before an adjective: 多大), 怎么 (how) and 怎么样 (how about) ask for a specific answer. The question word stays where the answer would go: 你叫什么名字？

几 is for small numbers and needs a measure word (几口人); 多少 is for any number (多少钱). The contrast example uses 吗, which makes a yes-no question instead; do not add 吗 to a question that already has a question word (you cannot say 你叫什么吗？).

examples.reading: nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?
examples.translation: How many people are there in your family?
How do we get to school?

lessons.title: Personal pronouns: 我 你 您 他 她 它 大家…
lessons.summary: Pronouns stand for people and things; 您 is polite, 它 is for things, 大家 addresses everyone.
pattern: 我 / 你 / 您 / 他 / 她 / 它 (+ 们)
body: 我 (I), 你 (you), 您 (you, polite), 他 (he), 她 (she), 它 (it) and their plurals with 们 (我们, 你们, 他们, 她们, 它们) stand for people and things. 您 shows respect (to a teacher or an older person). 它 is for things and animals. 大家 means everyone.

A singular pronoun cannot be summed up by 都: say 我们都去, not 我都去. The contrast example uses the suffix 们, which makes the plural (同学们); a number already gives the plural, so do not add 们 after it (三个学生, not 三个学生们).

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu yì zhī māo, tā hěn piàoliang.
examples.translation: I have a cat; it is pretty.

examples.text: 我姐姐是医生，她在医院工作。
examples.reading: wǒ jiějie shì yīshēng, tā zài yīyuàn gōngzuò.
examples.translation: My older sister is a doctor; she works in a hospital.

lessons.title: Demonstratives: 这 那 这儿 这些 有的…
lessons.summary: Point near (这) or far (那); 这儿/那儿 are places, 这些/那些 plural, 有的/有些 mean some.
pattern: 这 / 那 (+ 个 / 些 / 儿 / 里)
body: 这 (zhè, this) points near, 那 (nà, that) points far. 这儿 / 这里 and 那儿 / 那里 are places; 这个 / 那个 and 这些 / 那些 point to one or several things; 有的 and 有些 mean some (有的学生). A measure word usually follows 这 / 那 before a noun: 这本书, 那个电影.
The contrast example uses the question word 哪 (which), which asks rather than points and also needs a measure word (哪本书). 这 / 那 point; 哪 asks.

examples.reading: nǐ yào mǎi nǎ běn shū?
examples.translation: Which book do you want to buy?

lessons.title: Numerals: 一 二/两 三…十 百 千 半 零
lessons.summary: Count with numerals; use 两 (not 二) before a measure word, and 半 for half.
body: 一, 二, 三, 四, 五, 六, 七, 八, 九, 十, 百, 千 and 零 are the numerals. Before a measure word, two is 两, not 二: 两个人, 两本书. 二 is used inside numbers: 十二, 二十. 半 (bàn) means half: 半个苹果, 两点半. 零 marks an empty digit.

The contrast example uses the prefix 第, which makes an ordinal (第一 = first), not a count. 一 reads yī alone or at the end of a number (十一, 第一); before another syllable it changes: yí before a fourth tone (一个 yí ge, 第一个 dì-yí ge), yì before other tones (一本 yì běn, 第一本 dì-yì běn).

examples.reading: wǒ chī le bàn ge píngguǒ.

examples.translation: This phone costs a thousand yuan.

examples.reading: wǒ yì tiān chī sān ge píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I eat three apples a day.

examples.reading: tā shì wǒ de dì-yí ge péngyou.

lessons.title: Measure words: 本 个 家 口 块 件 只 元 杯
lessons.summary: A number or 这/那 needs a measure word before the noun; each noun takes its own.
pattern: numeral / 这 / 那 + measure word + noun
body: Between a number (or 这, 那, 几) and a noun, Chinese needs a measure word: 本 for books (一本书), 个 the general one (一个人), 家 for shops and families (两家饭店), 口 for family members (三口人), 块 for money and pieces (二十块), 件 for clothes and matters (一件衣服), 只 for animals (一只猫), 元 for money (formal). 杯 is borrowed from 杯子 for cups of drink (一杯茶).
The contrast example shows 两 before a measure word: before a measure word, two is 两, not 二 (两本书, not 二本书).

examples.reading: tā jiā yǒu sān zhī māo.
wǒ jiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
examples.translation: There are three people in my family.

examples.reading: wǒ hē le yì bēi chá.
examples.translation: I drank a cup of tea.

lessons.title: Time measure words: 日 号 岁 点 分 年 天
lessons.summary: Count dates, ages, clock time and durations with time measure words.
pattern: numeral + 岁 / 点 / 分 / 年 / 天 / 号 / 日
body: 岁 (suì) counts age (五岁); 号 and 日 name the day of the month (三月五号 / 三月五日); 点 and 分 tell the clock (八点, 八点十分); 年 and 天 count duration (一年, 三天). After a number, 年 and 天 need no extra measure word, but 月 takes 个 (三个月).
The contrast example uses 半 (half): 八点半 is half past eight, 半小时 is half an hour. 半 is a numeral, not a measure word.

examples.translation: Today is the fifth of March.

examples.reading: wǒ xué le yì nián Hànyǔ.
examples.translation: I studied Chinese for a year.

examples.reading: wǒ yì tiān gōngzuò bā ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: I work eight hours a day.

lessons.title: Degree adverbs: 非常 很 太 真 有点儿
lessons.summary: Put a degree adverb before an adjective; 太…了 exclamates, 有点儿 often signals a complaint.
pattern: subject + 非常 / 很 / 太 / 真 / 有点儿 + adjective
body: 非常 (fēicháng, very), 很 (hěn, very), 太 (tài, too), 真 (zhēn, really) and 有点儿 (yǒudiǎnr, a bit) go before an adjective: 非常热, 很好, 太贵了, 真好, 有点儿忙. 太 usually pairs with 了 to exclaim. 有点儿 often marks something unwanted.

The contrast example uses 一点儿, which measures a quantity of a thing (喝一点儿水) or follows a verb; it does not go before an adjective (you cannot say 一点儿忙). 有点儿 goes before an adjective; 一点儿 goes with a noun.

examples.translation: I would like to drink a little water.

lessons.title: 都: all, both
lessons.summary: 都 sums up the plural subject or the object placed before it; it comes before the verb.
body: 都 (dōu, all, both) sums up what comes before it: a plural subject (我们都去) or an object moved to the front (这些书我都看了). It stands after the subject and before the verb, never at the end.
The contrast example uses 也 (also), which adds one more rather than summing up all. With a singular subject, 都 is wrong (他都很忙 is not said); 也 is fine (他也很忙). When both appear, 也 comes first: 我们也都去.

examples.reading: zhèxiē shū wǒ dōu kàn le.
examples.translation: I have read all these books.

lessons.title: 在 and 正在: action in progress
lessons.summary: Put 在 or 正在 before the verb to say an action is happening now.
body: 在 (zài) and 正在 (zhèngzài) before a verb mark an action in progress: 我在吃饭, 妈妈正在做饭. 正在 stresses right now. This 在 is an adverb, different from the 在 that says where someone is (我在家).
The contrast example uses sentence-final 呢, which also marks an ongoing action (我吃饭呢) and can stand without 在. 了 marks a completed action, not an ongoing one.

lessons.title: 再: again, once more
lessons.summary: 再 before a verb says an action will happen again; it is for future repeats.
body: 再 (zài, again) before a verb says the action will repeat: 请再说一下, 我明天再来. It is used for future or intended repeats, not for a state that continues.

The contrast example uses 还 (still, more), which says a state continues or something is added. For still or in addition want, use 还, not 再: 我还想买一本书. 再 is for a future repeat of an action (再来, 再说一下). Do not confuse 再 with 在, which marks an action in progress.

examples.reading: nǐ zài chī yí ge bāozi ba.
wǒmen zài kàn yí ge diànyǐng.
wǒ hái xiǎng mǎi yì běn shū.
examples.translation: I still want to buy a book.

lessons.title: 还 and 也: also, still, more
lessons.summary: 也 adds (also); 还 adds more or says still; both come before the verb.
body: 也 (yě, also) adds one more of the same: 我也喜欢猫. 还 (hái, still, more) says a state continues or something is added: 他还有一个妹妹, 我还想喝茶. Both stand after the subject and before the verb.

The contrast example uses 都 (all), which sums up every member rather than adding one. When 也 and 都 appear together, 也 comes first: 我们也都想去. Do not put 也 or 还 after the verb or at the end of the sentence.

examples.reading: tā hái yǒu yí ge mèimei.
examples.translation: He also has a younger sister.
We all want to go too.

examples.text: 苹果很好吃，饺子也很好吃。
examples.reading: píngguǒ hěn hǎochī, jiǎozi yě hěn hǎochī.
examples.translation: Apples are tasty, and dumplings are tasty too.

lessons.title: Negation: 不 没(有) 不要
lessons.summary: 不 negates verbs and adjectives; 没(有) negates 有 and past events; 不要 forbids.
body: 不 (bù) negates a verb or adjective (我不喝茶, 今天不冷); before a fourth tone it is said bú (不是 bú shì). 没 / 没有 (méi / méiyǒu) negates 有 (我没有手机) and says a past event did not happen (昨天我没去学校). 不要 (bú yào) forbids: 请不要说话.

For a past event use 没, not 不, and drop 了 (我没吃饭, not 没吃了饭). The contrast example uses sentence-final 了 with 不 to mark a change of plan: 我不去了 (I am not going anymore). Do not put 了 right after a verb negated with 没. (不 occasionally appears in a past context with a refusing meaning, but at this level always use 没 for the past.)

examples.translation: I will not drink tea tomorrow.
I did not go to school yesterday.
He does not have a phone.
I do not want to go to work today.

lessons.title: 在: introducing time and place
lessons.summary: 在 + place comes before the verb to say where an action happens; time words also come before the verb.
body: The preposition 在 (zài) introduces a place before the verb: 我在家吃饭, 他在学校学习. A time word also comes before the verb: 我上午在医院看病. The place and time go before the action, not after it.

The contrast example uses the adverb 正在, which marks an action in progress (姐姐正在看电视), not a place. 在 can also be the verb to be at (我在家); here it is a preposition introducing where the action happens.

examples.translation: We have dinner at a restaurant.
I see a doctor at the hospital in the morning.
My older sister is watching TV.

lessons.title: Prepositions 和 and 对: introducing a person
lessons.summary: 和 introduces a companion (with); 对 introduces the target of an attitude (toward).
body: The preposition 和 (hé, with) introduces a companion before the verb: 我和他一起去学校. 对 (duì, toward) introduces the target of an attitude: 妈妈对我很好. Both come before the verb or adjective.

The contrast example uses 和 as a conjunction joining two nouns (苹果和饺子). As a preposition 和 means with and is followed by a verb phrase (我和朋友去); as a conjunction it joins two things into one unit (我喜欢苹果和饺子).

examples.reading: wǒ hé tā yìqǐ qù xuéxiào.
examples.translation: I go to school with him.
Mum is very kind to me.

examples.reading: wǒ hé jiějie zhù yí ge fángjiān.
examples.translation: I share a room with my older sister.
The teacher is very kind to us.

lessons.title: 和: joining words and phrases
lessons.summary: The conjunction 和 joins two nouns or phrases into one unit; it does not join sentences.
body: The conjunction 和 (hé, and) joins two nouns or phrases into one unit: 我和妹妹都喜欢猫, 我喜欢看书和写字. The joined unit acts as one subject or object.

The contrast example uses 和 as a preposition meaning with (我和朋友去电影院 = I go with friends). As a conjunction 和 joins two equal things; as a preposition it introduces a companion before a verb. 和 does not join two sentences (you cannot say 我去商店和我买书).

examples.reading: wǒ hé mèimei dōu xǐhuan māo.
examples.translation: My younger sister and I both like cats.

examples.text: 爸爸和妈妈都在公司工作。
examples.reading: bàba hé māma dōu zài gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.translation: Dad and Mum both work at a company.

examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan kàn shū hé xiě zì.

examples.text: 这本书和那本书都很好。
examples.reading: zhè běn shū hé nà běn shū dōu hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: This book and that book are both good.
I go to the cinema with a friend.

lessons.title: 的: linking a modifier to a noun
lessons.summary: 的 links an owner, adjective or clause to the noun it modifies.
body: 的 (de) links a modifier to a noun: possession (我的书), an adjective (大的苹果), or a clause (他写的字). With close people and groups it is often left out: 我妈妈, 我们学校.

The contrast example uses 得, which links a verb to a complement describing how the action is done (他说得很好). 的 goes before a noun; 得 goes after a verb. Do not use 的 to introduce a complement (说得好, not 说的很好).

examples.text: 我喜欢大的苹果，不喜欢小苹果。
examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan dà de píngguǒ, bù xǐhuan xiǎo píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I like big apples, not small ones.

examples.reading: tā xiě de zì hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: The characters he writes look nice.

lessons.title: 了: a completed action
lessons.summary: 了 after a verb marks that the action happened or is complete.
body: 了 (le) right after a verb marks a completed action: 我买了一本书, 他吃了三个饺子. To say it did not happen, use 没 and drop 了: 我没买.

The contrast example uses 过, which marks experience rather than a specific completed event (我没去过中国 = I have never been to China). After 没 use 过 for never (没去过), not 了 (you cannot say 没去了中国). 了 is for a specific finished action; 过 is for life experience.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū.
tā chī le sān ge jiǎozi.
wǒmen kàn le yí ge diànyǐng.
mèimei hē le yì bēi niúnǎi.
examples.translation: My younger sister drank a glass of milk.
I have never been to China.

lessons.title: Particles 吗 and 吧: questions and suggestions
lessons.summary: 吗 makes a yes-no question; 吧 makes a suggestion or a guess.
body: 吗 (ma) turns a statement into a yes-no question without changing the word order: 你是学生吗？ 吧 (ba) makes a suggestion (我们回家吧！= let us go home) or a guess (你是老师吧？= you are a teacher, right?).

The contrast example uses 呢, which cannot make a yes-no question. 呢 asks what about someone or something after a noun (我很好，你呢？= I am fine, and you?). Use 吗 for a yes-no question, 吧 for a suggestion or guess, 呢 for a follow-up.

lessons.title: Particles 了 and 呢: change and ongoing
lessons.summary: Sentence-final 了 announces a new situation; 呢 marks an ongoing action or softens a question.
body: At the end of a sentence 了 (le) announces that the situation has changed or come about: 下雨了 (it has started raining), 他会开车了 (he can drive now). 呢 (ne) marks an ongoing action (我吃饭呢 = I am eating) or softens a question with a question word (你在做什么呢？).

The contrast example uses 吗, which asks a yes-no question (你是医生吗？). 吗 does not combine with a question word or with 呢 (you cannot say 你在做什么吗？). Sentence-final 了 states a change; 呢 marks ongoing or a follow-up; 吗 asks yes-no.

lessons.title: 喂: hello on the phone
lessons.summary: 喂 is an interjection used to answer the phone or get someone's attention; it stands alone.
body: 喂 (wèi) is an interjection: it answers the phone or calls for attention (喂，你好！). It stands at the start, separated by a comma, and is not part of the sentence that follows. When answering the phone, many speakers say it with a rising tone, wéi; the dictionary lists wèi, and both are accepted.
The contrast example uses 请, which makes a polite request (请坐 = please sit). 喂 calls for attention; 请 asks someone politely to do something. Neither is a verb inside the sentence.

examples.translation: Hello, may I ask if he is in?
Hello, who are you looking for?

lessons.title: Basic phrase types: coordinate, modifier-head, verb-object, subject-predicate
lessons.summary: Phrases combine words: A和B, modifier+的+noun, verb+object, and subject+predicate.
body: Four basic phrase types: coordinate (我和妹妹, joined by 和), modifier-head (我的新书, a modifier before a noun), verb-object (看电影, a verb plus its object), and subject-predicate (他很好, a subject plus a predicate). Phrases combine into sentences.

The contrast example uses a preposition-object phrase (在家), which is an other type (next lesson): a preposition plus its object, used before a verb. The four basic types build the core of a sentence; preposition-object and place phrases modify it.

examples.translation: My younger sister and I go to school.

examples.reading: zhè shì wǒ de xīn shū.

examples.translation: I think he is very good.

lessons.title: Other phrase types: numeral-measure, preposition-object, place
lessons.summary: A numeral-measure phrase counts; a preposition-object phrase and a place phrase modify the verb.
body: Three other phrase types: numeral-measure (三本书, a number plus a measure word), preposition-object (在学校, 对我, a preposition plus its object), and place (桌子上, 家里, a noun plus a position word). They usually modify the verb or count a noun.
The contrast example uses a modifier-head phrase (弟弟的杯子), a basic type: a modifier before a noun. A numeral-measure phrase counts a noun; a modifier-head phrase describes whose or which noun it is.

examples.translation: The phone is on the table.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén.
examples.translation: There are five people in my family.
That is my younger brother's cup.

lessons.title: The subject: who or what the sentence is about
lessons.summary: A noun, pronoun or noun phrase can be the subject, before the predicate.
body: The subject is who or what the sentence is about. A noun (爸爸), a pronoun (我) or a noun phrase (我的老师, 这个商店) can be the subject. It comes before the predicate.
The contrast example uses the adverb 都, which is not part of the subject: it comes after the subject and before the verb (我们都喜欢他). Do not put 都 before the subject.

lessons.title: The predicate: what the subject does or is
lessons.summary: A verb, adjective or numeral-measure phrase can be the predicate; a noun predicate needs 是.
body: The predicate says what the subject does or is. A verb or verb phrase (吃米饭, 学习汉语), an adjective or adjective phrase (很冷), or a numeral-measure phrase (三岁) can be the predicate without 是.
The contrast example uses 是 for a noun predicate (他是医生). A noun cannot be the predicate on its own (you cannot say 他医生); it needs 是. An adjective does not take 是 (you cannot say 我是忙).

lessons.title: The object: what the action reaches
lessons.summary: A noun, pronoun or noun phrase can be the object, after the verb.
body: The object is what the action reaches. A noun (书), a pronoun (我) or a noun phrase (我的学校) can be the object. It comes after the verb: 看书, 认识我, 喜欢我的学校.
The contrast example uses a place phrase with 在, which comes before the verb, not as an object (弟弟在房间睡觉, not 弟弟睡觉在房间). Some verbs (睡觉, 上班) already contain their object and cannot take another.

examples.translation: My younger brother sleeps in the room.

lessons.title: The attributive: modifying a noun
lessons.summary: A noun word, adjective or numeral-measure phrase can modify a noun, often with 的.
body: The attributive modifies a noun: a noun word with 的 (我的书), an adjective (大苹果), or a numeral-measure phrase (两个姐姐). Some noun attributives drop 的 (汉语书, 我妈妈).
The contrast example uses 得, which introduces a complement after a verb (他汉语说得很好), not an attributive before a noun. 的 links a modifier to a noun; 得 links a verb to a complement.

examples.reading: nà shì māma de xīn yīfu.
tā Hànyǔ shuō de hěn hǎo.

lessons.title: The adverbial: modifying the verb
lessons.summary: An adverb, time word or place phrase can modify the verb, before it.
body: The adverbial modifies the verb or adjective: an adverb (很忙, 非常喜欢), a time word (明天去), or a place phrase (在家吃饭). It comes before the verb.

The contrast example uses 的, which links an attributive to a noun (姐姐的新手机), not an adverbial to a verb. An adverbial modifies the action; an attributive modifies a thing. Do not put the time or place after the verb.

examples.reading: zhè shì jiějie de xīn shǒujī.
examples.translation: This is my older sister's new phone.

lessons.title: Action-measure complement: counting an action
lessons.summary: 一下 (and 一次) after a verb counts how many times the action happens.
body: An action-measure complement counts occurrences of an action: 看一下, 问了一下. 一下 means once, a short try; 了 goes between the verb and 一下 (我看了一下). 一次 also means one time.
The contrast example uses 一点儿, which measures a quantity of a thing (喝一点儿水), not occurrences of an action. 一下 counts the action; 一点儿 measures the thing.

examples.reading: wǒ qù le yí cì yīyuàn.
examples.translation: I went to the hospital once.

lessons.title: Simple sentences: four predicate types
lessons.summary: A simple sentence has a verb, adjective, noun or no-subject predicate.
body: Four simple-sentence types by predicate: verb-predicate (他喜欢狗), adjective-predicate (今天天气很好), noun-predicate (今天星期三 — no 是 needed for dates and age), and non-subject-predicate (下雨了 — no subject).
The contrast example uses 是 for an identity sentence (我是学生). A noun-predicate sentence about date or age needs no 是; an identity or category sentence does need 是.

lessons.title: Declarative sentences: stating a fact
lessons.summary: A declarative states a fact with normal word order and ends in a period.
body: A declarative sentence states a fact: 我是学生, 他喜欢喝茶, 今天不冷. The word order is subject then predicate, and it ends in a period (。).

The contrast example uses 吗, which turns the same statement into a yes-no question (你会开车吗？) ending in a question mark. Adding 吗 changes a fact into a question; do not add it to a sentence you mean as a statement.

examples.translation: My younger sister is a student.
I do not have a younger brother.

lessons.title: Question types: yes-no, wh-, affirmative-negative
lessons.summary: Ask with 吗 (yes-no), a question word (wh-), or verb-not-verb (affirmative-negative).
body: Three question types: yes-no with 吗 (你是老师吗？), wh- with a question word in the answer position (你喝什么？, 这是谁的书？), and affirmative-negative with verb-not-verb (你去不去学校？). The affirmative-negative form does not take 吗.

The contrast example uses 呢 for a follow-up question (我喜欢猫，你呢？= and you?). 呢 asks what about someone; it is not a yes-no, wh- or affirmative-negative question. Do not add 吗 to a wh- or affirmative-negative question.

examples.translation: I like cats; what about you?

lessons.title: Imperative sentences: requests and commands
lessons.summary: 请 + verb makes a polite request; 不要 + verb forbids; the subject is often omitted.
body: An imperative gives a command or request. 请 (qǐng, please) makes it polite: 请大家坐, 请喝茶. 不要 (bú yào, do not) forbids: 不要说话, 不要看电视. The subject is usually left out.
The contrast example uses 吧, which softens a command into a suggestion (我们吃饭吧！= let us eat). 请 and 不要 address the listener directly; 吧 proposes doing something together.

lessons.title: Exclamative sentences: strong feeling
lessons.summary: 太…了！, 真…！ and 好…！ express strong feeling and end in an exclamation mark.
body: An exclamative expresses strong feeling: 太 + adjective + 了 (太好了！, 太热了！), 真 + adjective (真漂亮！), or 好 + adjective (好大的苹果！). It ends in an exclamation mark (！).
The contrast example uses 很 in a plain statement (今天很热。), which just describes without strong feeling. 太 usually needs 了 to exclaim; a bare 太热 is incomplete. 很 states a degree; 太 and 真 exclaim.

lessons.title: 是: A is B (identity or category)
lessons.summary: 是 links two nouns to say A is B; its negative is 不是.
body: 是 (shì) links two nouns to say A is B, an identity or category: 我是学生, 他是医生, 这是我的书. To negate, put 不 before it: 不是 (bú shì).
The contrast example uses 很 with an adjective (今天很冷). An adjective is a predicate on its own and does not take 是 (you cannot say 我是忙); 是 is for linking nouns, 很 is for describing with an adjective.

lessons.title: 有: possession
lessons.summary: 有 says someone has something; its negative is 没有, never 不有.
body: 有 (yǒu) says someone has something: 我有一个哥哥, 她有两只猫. Its negative is 没有 (méiyǒu), never 不有.
The contrast example uses 是 for identity (他是学生 = he is a student). 有 says what someone has (我有书); 是 says what someone or something is (这是书). Do not use 是 for possession or 有 for identity.

examples.translation: He does not have a car.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén.
examples.translation: There are five people in my family.

lessons.title: Existential sentences: what is at a place
lessons.summary: Place + 是 + noun identifies; place + 有 + numeral-measure + noun says what exists there.
body: An existential sentence introduces what is at a place. Place + 是 + noun identifies it (前边是一个书店); place + 有 + numeral-measure + noun says what exists there (桌子上有三本书).

The contrast example uses 在 with the thing first (书在桌子上), which says where the book is. An existential sentence puts the place first and introduces the thing; a 在 sentence puts the thing first and gives its place.

examples.translation: There is a teacher in front.

examples.reading: zhuōzi shàng yǒu sān běn shū.
examples.translation: There are three books on the table.

examples.reading: xuéxiào wàibian yǒu yí ge shāngdiàn.
examples.translation: There is a shop outside the school.
The book is on the table.

lessons.title: Serial-verb sentences: purpose or manner
lessons.summary: Two verbs share one subject: the second is the purpose of the first, or the first is the manner of the second.
body: In a serial-verb sentence two verbs share one subject and happen in order. The second action is the purpose of the first (我去商店买书 = I go to the shop to buy books); or the first is the manner of the second (他坐出租车去学校 = he goes to school by taxi).

The contrast example uses the preposition 和 (我和朋友去书店 = I go with a friend), which introduces a companion, not a second action. A serial-verb sentence has two actions by one subject; a 和 phrase has one action with a companion.

examples.translation: I go to the shop to buy books.
He goes to school by taxi.
Mum goes to the hospital to see a doctor.
I go to the bookshop with a friend.

lessons.title: Double-object sentences: verb + person + thing
lessons.summary: Some verbs take two objects: a person first, then a thing (给我一本书).
body: Some verbs take two objects: a person (the receiver) first, then a thing (what is given or asked). 给 (gěi, give): 我给你一本书. 问 (wèn, ask): 老师问我问题. The person comes before the thing.

The contrast example uses the preposition 对 (爸爸对我很好), which introduces the target of an attitude, not a transferred thing. A double-object verb transfers or asks something; 对 just points to whom an attitude is directed.

examples.reading: wǒ gěi nǐ yì běn shū.
wǒ wèn nǐ yí jiàn shì.
tā wèn wǒ jiào shénme míngzi.
examples.translation: He asks me what my name is.
Dad is very kind to me.

lessons.title: Coordinate clauses: …也…, …还…
lessons.summary: Two statements are joined by a comma with 也 or 还 in the second; no conjunction is needed.
body: A coordinate complex sentence joins two equal statements with a comma and 也 (also) or 还 (more) in the second: 我喜欢看书，也喜欢看电影; 他会说汉语，还会写汉字. No conjunction like and is needed.
The contrast example uses 和 to join two words inside one clause (我有哥哥和姐姐). 也 / 还 join two clauses; 和 joins words or phrases within one clause. Do not use 和 to join two sentences.

examples.text: 我喜欢看书，也喜欢看电影。
examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan kàn shū, yě xǐhuan kàn diànyǐng.
examples.translation: I like reading, and I also like watching films.

examples.text: 他会说汉语，还会写汉字。
examples.reading: tā huì shuō Hànyǔ, hái huì xiě Hànzì.
examples.translation: He can speak Chinese, and he can also write characters.

examples.reading: jīntiān hěn lěng, hái xià yǔ.
examples.translation: It is cold today, and it is also raining.

examples.reading: wǒ shì xuéshēng, tā yě shì xuéshēng.
examples.translation: I am a student, and he is a student too.
I have an older brother and an older sister.

lessons.title: Completed aspect: 了1
lessons.summary: 了1 right after the verb marks a completed action; negate with 没 and drop 了.
body: 了1 (le) right after the verb marks the action as completed: 我吃了两个苹果, 他写了一个字. It is about the action finishing, not about a change of situation.
The contrast example shows the negative: 我没吃饭. To say a completed action did not happen, use 没 and drop 了 (you cannot say 没吃了饭). 不 is for habits or the future, not for a past completed action.

examples.reading: wǒ chī le liǎng ge píngguǒ.
tā xiě le yí ge zì.
wǒmen hē le yì bēi chá.
examples.translation: We drank a cup of tea.

examples.reading: mèimei chuān le yí jiàn xīn yīfu.
examples.translation: My younger sister put on new clothes.

lessons.title: Change aspect: 了2
lessons.summary: Sentence-final 了2 marks a new situation or a change: it is so now.
body: 了2 (le) at the end of a sentence marks a new situation or change: 天冷了 (it has got cold), 我会说汉语了 (I can speak Chinese now), 他不去学校了 (he is not going to school anymore). It is about the situation now, not about one finished action.

The contrast example uses 了1 right after the verb (我买了一个苹果), which marks a completed action. 了1 follows the verb and marks completion; 了2 ends the sentence and marks change. Both can appear together, but they do different jobs.

examples.translation: He is not going to school anymore.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le yí ge píngguǒ.

lessons.title: Progressive aspect: 在/正在…呢
lessons.summary: 在/正在 before the verb, or 呢 at the end, marks an action in progress.
body: The progressive marks an action in progress: 在 / 正在 before the verb (我在看书, 爸爸正在打电话), 呢 at the end (他吃饭呢), or both (妹妹在睡觉呢).

The contrast example uses 了1 (我吃了两个包子), which marks a completed action. The progressive says the action is happening now; 了 says it is finished. They mark different aspects and are not used for the same meaning.

examples.reading: wǒ chī le liǎng ge bāozi.

lessons.title: Number expressions: money and ordinals
lessons.summary: Money is number + 块 (spoken) or 元 (formal); ordinals are 第 + number.
body: Money: number + 块 (kuài, spoken) or 元 (yuán, formal): 二十块, 一千元. Ordinals: 第 + number: 第一 (first), 第二 (second). 第 makes an order, not a count.
The contrast example uses 两 before a measure word (我有两个哥哥). Before a measure word, two is 两, not 二; 第 + number is an ordinal, while a bare number counts.

examples.translation: This phone is a thousand yuan.

examples.reading: zhè shì wǒ dì-yì tiān shàngbān.
examples.translation: This is my first day at work.
A cup of tea is ten yuan.

lessons.title: Time expressions: dates, weekdays and clock time
lessons.summary: Dates run year-month-day, weekdays are 星期 + number, and clock time is number + 点 + 分.
body: Dates run from big to small: year + 月 + 日 / 号 (三月五号). Weekdays are 星期 + number (星期一 to 星期六, 星期日 / 星期天). Clock time is number + 点 + number + 分 (八点十分). 号 is spoken, 日 is written.
The contrast example uses 半 (half): 现在两点半 (it is half past two). 半 marks the half hour; 分 marks minutes. Both come after 点.

examples.translation: I am going to China next year.
He has class in the morning.

lessons.title: 后缀 -面: 上面 下面 前面 后面 里面 外面
lessons.summary: -面 attaches to position words to make a side or place word: 上面, 下面, 里面.
pattern: 上 / 下 / 前 / 后 / 里 / 外 + 面
body: 面 (miàn) is a suffix that makes a side or place word: 上面 (above), 下面 (below), 前面 (in front), 后面 (behind), 里面 (inside), 外面 (outside). With 在 it names where something is: 书在桌子上面.

The contrast example uses 边, which makes place words the same way (门边, 桌子上边). 边 and 面 are different words; learn each place word as a whole and do not mix them, so 旁边 not 旁面, and 桌子上面 or 桌子上边 rather than a blend.

examples.translation: The book is on the table.

examples.reading: xuéxiào hòumian yǒu yí ge gōngyuán.
examples.translation: There is a park behind the school.
The cat is by the door.

lessons.title: 左 and 右: 左边 右边
lessons.summary: 左 and 右 name sides; add 边 to make 左边 and 右边.
pattern: 在 + noun + 左边 / 右边
body: 左 (zuǒ, left) and 右 (yòu, right) name sides. With a noun they make a place phrase: 桌子左边 (to the left of the table), 学校右边; add 边 to make 左边 / 右边, which can also stand alone: 往左看 (look left), 你的右边.
The contrast example uses 往, which introduces a direction you move toward (往右转), while 左边 / 右边 name a place (在桌子左边). A place word follows 在; a direction word follows 往.

examples.translation: The bank is to the left of the school.

examples.reading: wǒ de jiā zài chāoshì yòubian.
examples.translation: My home is to the right of the supermarket.

lessons.title: Reduplicated verbs: 看看 问一问 看了看
lessons.summary: Repeat a verb to say an action is brief or casual: 看看, 试一试, 看了看.
pattern: V + V: 看看, 想想
V + 一 + V: 试一试; V + 了 + V: 看了看
body: Single-syllable verbs can be reduplicated to say do something a little or casually: 看看, 想想, 听听. A一A puts 一 in the middle: 试一试, 问一问. A了A puts 了 in the middle: 看了看, 试了试. Two-syllable verbs repeat the whole word: 学习学习, 讨论讨论. Verbs like 是, 有 and 在 do not reduplicate.
The contrast example uses 一下 after the verb (请看一下). 一下 also makes an action brief, but the verb itself is not repeated: 看一下 is not 看一看.

lessons.title: 可能: maybe, possibly
lessons.summary: Put 可能 before the verb to say something is possible.
body: 可能 (kěnéng) says something is possible: 他可能来, 明天可能下雨, 这件事可能很难. It can also start a short answer: 可能. Negate with 不可能 (impossible); do not say 不可 here.
The contrast example uses 会, which says a skill or a future fact rather than doubt: 他会说汉语. 可能 tells the listener the speaker is not sure.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì kěnéng hěn nán.

lessons.title: 离合词: 帮忙 游泳 跳舞 跑步
lessons.summary: These verbs contain their object; put 了, 个 or a duration between the two parts.
pattern: 帮 + 忙: 帮个忙, 请他帮忙
游 + 泳 / 跳 + 舞: 游了一个小时泳
跑 + 步: 跑了一会儿步
body: 帮忙, 游泳, 跳舞 and 跑步 are separable: 帮+忙, 游+泳, 跳+舞, 跑+步. Put 了, 个 or a duration between the parts: 帮个忙, 我请他帮忙, 游了一个小时泳, 跳了一支舞, 跑了一会儿步. Do not put another object after the whole verb: 帮忙朋友 is wrong.
The contrast example uses the plain verb 帮, which takes a person as its object: 妈妈帮我. 帮忙 is a separable unit, so you say 帮我一个忙, not 帮忙我.

examples.reading: tā yóu le yí ge xiǎoshí yǒng.
tā tiào le yì zhī wǔ.

lessons.title: 为什么: why
lessons.summary: 为什么 asks for a reason; answer with 因为.
body: 为什么 (wèishénme, why) asks for a reason: 你为什么迟到？ 他为什么不来？ Do not add 吗 after it: 你为什么不来吗？ is wrong.
The contrast example answers with 因为: 因为天气不好. 为什么 asks, 因为 answers; the answer to 为什么 is usually a reason clause, not a thing.

examples.translation: Why do you not drink tea?

lessons.title: 自己: self, by oneself
lessons.summary: A pronoun plus 自己 stresses that person: 我自己, 你自己.
body: 自己 (zìjǐ) follows a pronoun or a name to stress that person: 我自己, 你自己, 他自己. It can stand alone as the subject: 自己的事情自己做. When the subject and object are the same person, use 自己: 他喜欢自己看书.
The contrast example uses 我们 without 自己. A pronoun alone is the plain subject; adding 自己 stresses that these people do it themselves, not someone else.

examples.translation: I go to school by myself.

examples.reading: nǐ zìjǐ zuò fàn, hǎo ma?

lessons.title: 这么 那么 这样 那样 每
lessons.summary: 这么/那么 show degree; 这样/那样 show manner; 每 means every.
pattern: 这么 / 那么 + adjective / verb
body: 这么 (zhème, so) and 那么 (nàme, so) go before an adjective or a verb to show degree: 这么大, 那么好, 那么喜欢. 这样 (like this) and 那样 (like that) describe manner: 这样做, 那样想. 每 (měi, every) goes with a measure word: 每天, 每个.
The contrast example uses 很, a plain degree adverb: 今天很冷. 这么 and 那么 say so much, often pointing at something or matching a comparison; 很 just gives the degree without that reference.

examples.translation: Let us do it like this.

lessons.title: Reduplicated adjectives: 大大的 高高兴兴
lessons.summary: Double an adjective for a vivid, warm tone: AA的 or AABB的.
pattern: AA + 的: 大大的, 红红的
AABB + 的: 干干净净的
AABB + 地 + verb: 高高兴兴地
body: Single-syllable adjectives can double to AA, usually with 的: 高高的, 大大的, 红红的. Two-syllable adjectives often become AABB: 高高兴兴, 干干净净, 清清楚楚. A reduplicated adjective goes before the noun with 的 (大大的眼睛) or before the verb with 地 (高高兴兴地回家).
The contrast example uses 很: 这件衣服很漂亮. 很 states a degree; reduplication paints a picture and sounds warmer or more casual. Say 很漂亮, not 很漂漂亮亮.

examples.reading: wǒmen gāogāo xìngxìng de huí jiā.

lessons.title: Numbers: 万 好多 多
lessons.summary: 万 is ten thousand; 好多 means a lot; 多 with a noun means many.
body: 万 (wàn) is ten thousand: 一万, 三万; after a number it acts as the unit. 好多 (hǎoduō) means a lot of: 好多书, 好多学生. 多 (duō) before a noun means many: 很多人; in questions it becomes 多少: 多少人.
The contrast example uses 几, which asks for a small approximate number and needs a measure word: 几个朋友. 多少 asks for any amount; 几 expects a small one.

examples.text: 我们学校有一万个学生。
examples.reading: wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu yí wàn ge xuéshēng.
examples.translation: Our school has ten thousand students.
There are lots of people in the park.
How many students are there in your class?
How many friends do you have?

lessons.title: Measure words: 条 位 间 名 包
lessons.summary: 条 for long things, 位 politely for people, 间 for rooms, 名 for roles, 包 for bags.
pattern: numeral + 条 / 位 / 间 / 名 / 包 + noun
body: 条 (tiáo) counts long, thin things: 一条鱼, 一条路, 一条裤子. 位 (wèi) counts people politely: 一位老师, 两位朋友. 间 (jiān) counts rooms: 一间教室, 两间卧室. 名 (míng) counts people in roles: 一名学生, 两名医生. 包 (bāo) is borrowed from the bag: 一包饼干.
The contrast example uses 个, the general measure from Level 1: 一个书包. Use a specific measure when the noun calls for one, and keep the pair noun and measure together.

examples.reading: tā mǎi le yì tiáo yú.

lessons.title: 次: times, occasions
lessons.summary: 次 counts how many times: 一次, 两次, 三次.
body: 次 (cì) counts occasions: 一次 (once), 两次 (twice), 三次 (three times). Put the number and 次 after the verb: 去了一次北京, 看了两次电影. With 过 it counts past experiences: 我去过两次北京. It does not count how long; use a duration such as 一个小时 for that.
The contrast example uses 一下: 我看了一下表. 一下 makes an action brief and is not counted; 次 counts the number of times.

examples.reading: wǒ qù guo yí cì Běijīng.
examples.translation: I have been to Beijing once.

examples.reading: tā kàn le liǎng cì zhè bù diànyǐng.
wǒmen jiàn guo yí cì miàn.
wǒ kàn le yí xià biǎo.
examples.translation: I took a look at my watch.

lessons.title: 多 好 最: exclamation and superlative
lessons.summary: 多 and 好 exclaim before an adjective; 最 picks the highest degree.
body: 多 (duō) before an adjective makes an exclamation: 多甜啊, 多美！ 好 (hǎo) in exclamations means very: 好冷啊, 好漂亮！ 最 (zuì, most) makes the superlative: 最好, 最多, 他最高. Do not put 很 before 最.
The contrast example uses 很: 今天很热. 很 states a degree without exclaiming; 多 and 好 carry feeling, and 最 compares one thing with all others.

examples.reading: tā shì wǒmen bān zuì gāo de.
examples.translation: He is the tallest in our class.

lessons.title: 一起: together
lessons.summary: 一起 goes after the subject and before the verb to say people do something together.
pattern: A 和 B + 一起 + verb
body: 一起 (yìqǐ, together) stands after the subject and before the verb: 我们一起吃早饭. With two people, join them with 和: 我和爸爸一起看电视. It is an adverb, so it does not stand at the end of the sentence.
The contrast example uses 和 alone: 我和妹妹一起回家. 和 joins two people into one subject; 一起 says they act together. In 我和妹妹一起回家 both are present, and the order of 我 and 妹妹 can be swapped.

examples.reading: wǒ hé bàba yìqǐ kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: Dad and I watch television together.
The classmates go to the library together.

examples.reading: wǒ hé mèimei yìqǐ huí jiā.
examples.translation: My sister and I go home together.

lessons.title: Time adverbs: 还 已经 有时 快 正要
lessons.summary: 还 says still; 已经 says already; 有时 says sometimes; 快/快要 say soon; 正 says just now.
pattern: 有时(候) + clause; 快 / 快要 + … + 了
body: 还 (hái, still) says a situation continues: 他还在睡觉. 已经 (yǐjīng, already): 我已经做完作业了. 有时 / 有时候 says occasionally: 我有时候去公园. 快 and 快要 say something is about to happen, usually with 了: 天快下雨了, 快要过年了. 正 stresses the exact moment: 他正看书呢.
The contrast example uses 现在, a time noun: 他现在在看书. 现在 says when; 在 / 正在 / 正 are adverbs placed before the verb. Both 现在我在看书 and 我现在在看书 are possible orders.

examples.reading: wǒ yǐjīng zuò wán zuòyè le.
examples.translation: I have already finished my homework.
I sometimes go to the park.

lessons.title: 常 and 经常: often
lessons.summary: 常常 and 经常 before the verb mean often; 常 is the short written form.
pattern: subject + 常常 / 经常 + verb
body: 常常 (chángcháng) and 经常 (jīngcháng) mean often and stand before the verb: 我经常去图书馆, 他常常迟到. 常 is the short written form: 常来, 常去. Both describe a habit, not a single occasion.
The contrast example uses 有时: 我有时去公园. 经常 / 常常 mean often or regularly; 有时 means sometimes, so the frequency is lower.

examples.translation: I often go to the library.
Grandfather often goes to the park.
I sometimes go to the park.

lessons.title: 别: do not, don't
lessons.summary: 别 before a verb makes a negative command: 别说话.
body: 别 (bié) is the spoken negative command: 别说, 别走, 别忘了. It tells someone not to do something now or later. It cannot negate the past; say 昨天我没去, not 昨天别去.
The contrast example uses 不要: 请不要在这里抽烟. 别 and 不要 both make negative commands; 别 is shorter and more spoken, 不要 is fuller and common in notices and writing.

examples.translation: Do not forget to bring the book.

examples.reading: qǐng búyào zài zhèlǐ chōu yān.

lessons.title: 再 and 就 linking actions
lessons.summary: 再 says then / next after something else; 就 says then / as early as.
body: 再 as a connective says then after something else: 我先喝水，再吃饭. 就 says an action follows soon or early: 他一来我就走; 我五点就起床. Both link two clauses.
The contrast example uses 才: 他十点才起床. 就 says early or quick; 才 says late or not until, so 就五点 and 才十点 point in opposite directions.

examples.reading: wǒ xiān hē shuǐ, zài chī fàn.
examples.translation: I will drink some water first, then eat.

examples.reading: tā yì lái wǒ jiù zǒu.
examples.translation: As soon as he comes, I will leave.

examples.reading: wǒ wǔ diǎn jiù qǐ chuáng.
examples.translation: I get up as early as five.

examples.reading: tā shí diǎn cái qǐ chuáng.
examples.translation: He did not get up until ten.

lessons.title: 都 就 还是: attitude words
lessons.summary: 都 stresses even; 就 stresses exactly or just; 还是 suggests or says still.
body: 都 adds emphasis, often with 了: 他都十二岁了. 就 narrows or fixes: 我就想去公园 (that is all I want), 他就十块钱 (exactly ten kuai). 还是 suggests or says something remains: 还是你先去吧, 他还是在睡觉.
The contrast example uses 也: 他也很想去. 都 sums up or stresses even; 也 adds one more. With a singular subject 都 is wrong (say 他也想去, not 他都很想去).

examples.translation: I just want to go to the park.

lessons.title: 从: from (time and place)
lessons.summary: 从 marks the start of a time or place span; 到 marks the end.
body: 从 (cóng) marks a starting point in space or time: 我从中国来, 从早上到晚上, 从家到学校. It is often paired with 到: 从一楼到三楼. For a pure location use 在, not 从.
The contrast example uses 在: 书在桌子上. 从 introduces where something starts or comes from; 在 says where it is.

examples.reading: cóng zǎoshang dào wǎnshang, tā gōngzuò.
examples.translation: He works from morning till night.

examples.reading: cóng jiā dào xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.translation: It is very close from home to school.
The book is on the table.

lessons.title: 往 and 从: direction and route
lessons.summary: 往 says toward; 从 says by way of / through.
body: 往 (wǎng) says toward a direction: 往前走, 往左看, 往回走. 从 (cóng) here says by way of or through: 从这条路走, 从桥上过去. 往 is the direction you face or head; 从 is the route taken.
The contrast example uses 到: 我们到学校了. 往 points in a direction; 到 names the place you arrive at.

examples.reading: wǒmen cóng zhè tiáo lù zǒu.

lessons.title: 给 比 跟: objects
lessons.summary: 给 introduces the receiver; 比 compares; 跟 introduces the person you act with.
body: 给 (gěi) introduces the receiver: 给他一本书, 给妈妈打电话. 比 (bǐ) compares: 他比我高, 我比弟弟大. 跟 (gēn) introduces the person you do something with: 跟我来, 跟他说话.
The contrast example uses 对: 爸爸对我很好. 跟 says together or with; 对 says an attitude or action is directed toward someone, and it does not take a following verb phrase the same way.

examples.reading: wǒ gěi tā yì běn shū.

examples.translation: Dad is very kind to me.

lessons.title: 因为: because
lessons.summary: 因为 introduces a reason; often paired with 所以.
body: 因为 (yīnwèi) introduces a reason clause: 因为下雨, 因为我不舒服. It can answer a question alone: 为什么不来？因为下雨. Often it pairs with 所以 (therefore): 因为下雨，所以我不去.
The contrast example uses 所以: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少. 因为 gives the reason, 所以 gives the result; do not reverse them.

examples.reading: yīnwèi xià yǔ, wǒ méiyǒu qù.
examples.translation: Because it rained, I did not go.

examples.reading: yīnwèi shēngbìng, tā méi lái shàngkè.
examples.translation: Because he was ill, he did not come to class.

examples.text: 因为冷，我穿了很多衣服。
examples.reading: yīnwèi lěng, wǒ chuān le hěnduō yīfu.
examples.translation: Because it was cold, I put on many clothes.

examples.text: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià xuě, suǒyǐ lù shang rén hěn shǎo.
examples.translation: Because it snowed, there were few people on the road.

lessons.title: 跟 joining words: A 跟 B
lessons.summary: 跟 connects two nouns as a compound subject or object, like 和.
body: 跟 (gēn) can join two nouns like 和: 老师跟学生一起去, 我跟你. It is more spoken and northern; 和 is the general form. Do not use 跟 to join clauses; use punctuation or a clause conjunction such as 但是.
The contrast example uses 和: 我喜欢苹果和梨. 和 is neutral and works anywhere; 跟 as a conjunction is informal and joins nouns or pronouns, not whole clauses.

examples.text: 老师跟学生一起去公园。
examples.reading: lǎoshī gēn xuéshēng yìqǐ qù gōngyuán.
examples.translation: The teacher and the students go to the park together.
I will go together with you.

examples.text: 哥哥跟弟弟都喜欢踢足球。
examples.reading: gēge gēn dìdi dōu xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
examples.translation: Both the older and the younger brother like playing football.

lessons.title: Clause conjunctions: 但是 那 虽然 还是
lessons.summary: 这些连词连接分句：但是转折，那承接，虽然/还是让步。
body: 但 and 但是 turn to a contrasting second clause: 我很喜欢这本书，但是太贵了. 那 carries on: 那你就别去了. 虽然 concedes: 虽然下雨，我还是去; 还是 after 虽然 says still. 因为 and 所以 join cause and result: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少.
The contrast example uses 那 as a demonstrative: 那个人是我的老师. 那 before a noun points at something (Level 1); 那 between clauses is the conjunction. The two 那 have the same shape but different jobs.

examples.text: 我很喜欢这本书，但是太贵了。
examples.reading: wǒ hěn xǐhuan zhè běn shū, dànshì tài guì le.
examples.translation: I like this book a lot, but it is too expensive.

examples.reading: nà nǐ jiù bié qù le.

examples.text: 虽然下雨，我们还是去了。
examples.reading: suīrán xià yǔ, wǒmen háishì qù le.
examples.translation: Although it rained, we still went.

examples.reading: nàge rén shì wǒ de lǎoshī.

lessons.title: 得 and 地: complement and adverbial markers
lessons.summary: 得 after a verb introduces a complement; 地 after an adjective marks how an action is done.
body: 得 (de) after a verb introduces a description of the action: 说得很好, 跑得很快. 地 (de) after an adjective or adverb modifies the verb: 慢慢地走, 高兴地说. Both are read neutral in these positions.
The contrast example uses 的: 这是我的书. 的 before a noun marks possession or attribution; 得 follows a verb; 地 comes before a verb it modifies. The same sound has three different jobs.

lessons.title: 过: past experience
lessons.summary: Verb + 过 says the action has happened at least once; negate with 没(有)…过.
body: 过 (guo) after a verb marks an experience in the past: 我去过中国, 你吃过烤鸭吗. To say it never happened, put 没(有) before the verb and keep 过 after it: 我没去过上海. Do not use 不 here.
The contrast example uses 了: 我吃了两个苹果. 过 says the speaker has had the experience at some time; 了 says the action was completed on that occasion.

examples.reading: nǐ chī guo Běijīng kǎoyā ma?
examples.translation: Have you ever eaten Peking duck?
I have never been to Shanghai.

examples.reading: wǒ chī le liǎng ge píngguǒ.

lessons.title: 着: continuing state
lessons.summary: Verb + 着 says a state holds or a posture continues: 门开着, 他拿着一本书.
body: 着 (zhe) after a verb marks a continuing state or posture: 门开着, 他穿着一件白衬衫, 他拿着一本书. It often describes a scene or background: 墙上挂着一幅画 (see 存现句).
The contrast example uses 在: 他在看书. 着 describes a state that holds; 在 / 正在 describe an action happening now. 门开着 is a state, 门在开 is an action in progress.

examples.reading: tā ná zhe yì běn shū.
tā chuān zhe yí jiàn bái chènshān.
examples.translation: She is wearing a white shirt.

lessons.title: 呢 吧 的 啊: sentence-final particles
lessons.summary: 呢 asks or marks ongoing; 吧 suggests; 的 confirms; 啊 exclaims or softens.
body: 呢 (ne) asks a follow-up question or marks an ongoing state: 你呢？, 他吃饭呢. 吧 (ba) softens a suggestion or guess: 我们走吧, 是吧. 的 (de) confirms: 他会来的. 啊 (a) exclaims or softens: 真好啊, 快来啊.
The contrast example uses 吗: 你是学生吗？ 吗 makes a plain yes-no question; 呢 / 吧 / 的 / 啊 each color the sentence differently and cannot replace 吗 there.

lessons.title: Verb-complement phrases: V + result/degree
lessons.summary: A complement follows the verb and adds its result or degree: 看见, 做完, 听懂.
pattern: V + complement: 看 + 见, 做 + 完
body: In a verb-complement phrase the second part tells what happens to the action: 看见 (see and perceive), 听懂 (listen and understand), 做完 (finish doing), 看清楚. It is different from a verb-object phrase, where the second part is the thing acted on: 看书, 吃饭.
The contrast example uses a verb-object phrase: 我吃饭. 吃饭 takes a thing (the object); 做完 takes a result (the complement).

lessons.title: Phrases: …的, serial verbs, pivotal phrases
lessons.summary: 的字短语 stands for a thing; 连谓短语 chains verbs; 兼语短语 shares one person between verbs.
pattern: 请/让 + person + V (兼语短语)
body: 的字短语: 的 after a phrase stands for a thing or person: 我的, 红色的, 卖菜的. 连谓短语: two verbs share one subject and happen together or in order: 去买菜, 笑着说. 兼语短语: the object of the first verb is also the subject of the second: 请他来, 让我走.
The contrast example uses 和: 我有哥哥和姐姐. 和 joins two nouns into one phrase; it does not chain verbs or make a pivotal structure.

examples.translation: I have an older brother and an older sister.

lessons.title: Phrase functions: noun, verb, adjective
lessons.summary: A phrase can act as a noun, a verb or an adjective: 新书, 去买菜, 很大.
pattern: 名词性: 新的书 / 我的书
动词性: 去买菜 / 喜欢看书
形容词性: 很大 / 红红的
body: By function, a phrase can behave like a noun (名词性: 一本新书, 我的书), like a verb (动词性: 去买菜, 喜欢看书), or like an adjective (形容词性: 很大, 干干净净的). Function depends on the head word and on where the phrase sits in the sentence.
The contrast example uses 的: 我的书在桌子上. 的 turns pronoun plus noun into a noun phrase; without 的 you cannot put those two words together as one modifier.

examples.reading: zhè shì yì běn xīn shū.
wǒ de shū zài zhuōzi shàng.
examples.translation: My book is on the table.

lessons.title: 什么的: and so on
lessons.summary: 什么的 follows a list to mean and so on: 苹果、香蕉什么的.
body: 什么的 (shénme de) follows one or more items to mean and so on: 我喜欢吃苹果、香蕉什么的; 他买了书、本子什么的. It is informal. Do not use 什么的 when only one item is named, and do not mix it with 等.
The contrast example uses 和: 我喜欢苹果和梨. 和 links exactly two items; 什么的 closes a list of two or more and adds and so on.

examples.reading: tā mǎi le shū, běnzi shénme de.
examples.translation: He bought books, notebooks and so on.

examples.text: 我喜欢唱歌、跳舞什么的。
examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan chànggē, tiàowǔ shénme de.
examples.translation: I like singing, dancing and so on.

examples.text: 周末我常看书、运动什么的。
examples.reading: zhōumò wǒ cháng kàn shū, yùndòng shénme de.
examples.translation: At weekends I often read, exercise and so on.

lessons.title: 还是……吧: a gentle suggestion
lessons.summary: 还是……吧 suggests an option after thinking it over: 我们还是走吧.
body: 还是……吧 makes a gentle suggestion or a choice after weighing things: 我们还是坐出租车去吧, 你还是先吃饭吧. It softens advice; 吧 alone can also suggest, but 还是…吧 adds an afterthought.
The contrast example uses 好吗: 我们明天去，好吗？ 好吗 asks whether the listener agrees; 还是…吧 recommends one option instead of asking.

examples.reading: nǐ háishì xiān chī fàn ba.
wǒmen háishì zuò dìtiě qù ba.
examples.translation: We had better go by underground.

lessons.title: 要……了: about to happen
lessons.summary: 要/快要/就要…了 says something is just going to happen.
pattern: 快要 / 就要 + V + 了
body: 要…了, 快要…了 and 就要…了 all say an event is about to happen: 要下雨了, 火车快要到了, 他就要回来了. Add 了 at the end. 快要 is one word; 就要 stresses that the time is right.
The contrast example uses 已经: 他已经回家了. 已经 says the event already happened; 要 / 快要 say it has not happened yet.

examples.translation: He is about to come back.

lessons.title: 都……了: lateness or amount
lessons.summary: 都……了 stresses that something is later or larger than expected.
body: 都……了 stresses surprise or lateness: 都十点了，快睡吧; 他都十八岁了; 都三点了，他还没来. It sums up the scale and adds 了. This is not the 都 that sums people before the verb (我们都去).
The contrast example uses 已经: 我已经吃过了. 已经 simply says already; 都…了 adds surprise that it is so late or so much.

examples.reading: dōu shí diǎn le, kuài shuì ba.
examples.translation: It is already ten o'clock; go to sleep.

examples.reading: dōu sān diǎn le, tā hái méi lái.
examples.translation: It is already three, and he has not come.

lessons.title: Patient subjects: the thing comes first
lessons.summary: In a patient-subject sentence the thing receives the action: 作业做完了.
body: In a patient-subject sentence the subject is the thing the action happens to: 作业做完了, 苹果吃完了, 这本书我看过了. The doer can be left out because it is known or unimportant. This is not the passive with 被 (Level 3).

The contrast example uses the doer as subject: 我做完了作业. A patient-subject sentence puts the thing first (受事主语); an ordinary sentence puts the doer first (施事主语). Both orders are possible here, so the word-order exercise is skipped.

examples.reading: zhè běn shū wǒ kàn guo le.

lessons.title: Noun-phrase predicates
lessons.summary: A noun phrase can be the predicate directly: 今天星期三, 他北京人.
body: With dates, weekdays, places and origins, Chinese often drops 是 and puts a noun phrase directly after the subject: 今天星期三, 他北京人, 明天晴天. Adding 是 is possible and more formal: 今天是星期三.

The contrast example uses 是: 他是老师. 是 equates the subject with the noun; the noun-phrase predicate without 是 is used for classification details such as date, origin and weather, and sounds more spoken.

lessons.title: Attributives: verb phrases and subject-predicate phrases
lessons.summary: A verb phrase or subject-predicate phrase can modify a noun with 的: 我买的书, 身体好的学生.
body: An attributive (定语) comes before the noun and usually takes 的: 我买的书, 昨天来的客人. A subject-predicate phrase can also be an attributive: 身体好的学生, 天气冷的冬天. Some short attributives drop 的: 汉语老师.
The contrast example uses 地: 他高兴地说. An attributive with 的 goes before a noun; an adverbial with 地 goes before a verb. Check what follows the marker, not just the sound.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi de shū hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: The book I bought is very good.

examples.text: 昨天来的客人是我的老师。
examples.reading: zuótiān lái de kèren shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.translation: The guest who came yesterday is my teacher.

examples.text: 身体好的学生都很努力。
examples.reading: shēntǐ hǎo de xuéshēng dōu hěn nǔlì.
examples.translation: Students in good health all work hard.

lessons.title: Result complements: 错 懂 好 会 完
lessons.summary: A result complement after the verb says how the action turns out: 做完, 听懂.
pattern: V + 完 / 好 / 懂 / 会 / 错
body: 完 (finish), 好 (done well or ready), 懂 (understand), 会 (know how) and 错 (wrong) follow the verb as results: 写完, 做好, 听懂, 学会, 做错. To say the result did not happen, insert 不: 听不懂, 做不完; with 得 it says possibility: 听得懂, 做得完.
The contrast example uses 得: 他说得很好. A result complement attaches the outcome directly to the verb; 得 introduces a description of manner or degree.

examples.reading: wǒ tīng dǒng lǎoshī de huà le.
examples.translation: I understood what the teacher said.

lessons.title: Simple directional complements
lessons.summary: A one-syllable direction word follows the verb: 寄来, 上楼, 走进.
pattern: V + 进 / 出 / 回 / 过
body: 简单趋向补语 is one syllable after the verb: 来 toward the speaker, 去 away, 上 up or onto, 下 down or off, 进 into, 出 out of, 回 back, 过 across, 起 up. With a thing object, put the complement before the object: 寄来一封信, 拿回来一本书.
The contrast example uses the compound 上来: 他走上来了. A compound has two syllables (上 + 来); a simple complement has one (上 or 来). Learn them as separate words.

examples.reading: tā jì lái yì fēng xìn.

lessons.title: Compound directional complements
lessons.summary: Two-syllable complements combine directions: 上来, 下来, 进来, 出来, 回来.
pattern: V + 下来 / 下去; V + 起来
V + 进来 / 进去; V + 出来 / 出去; V + 回来 / 过来
body: 复合趋向补语 combines two directions: 上 + 来 = 上来, 下 + 去 = 下去, 进 + 来 = 进来, 出 + 去 = 出去, 回 + 来 = 回来, 过 + 来 = 过来, 起 + 来 = 起来. The second syllable points relative to the speaker: 来 toward, 去 away.
The contrast example uses the simple 上: 他走上楼了. 上 alone is a simple complement; 上来 is its compound form. Both describe movement, but they are different words.

examples.text: 他从楼上拿下来一本书。
examples.reading: tā cóng lóu shàng ná xiàlai yì běn shū.
examples.translation: He brought a book down from upstairs.

lessons.title: State complements: V + 得 + adjective
lessons.summary: 得 after a verb describes how the action is done: 说得很好, 跑得很快.
pattern: V + 得 + 很 / 非常 + adj
body: 得 (de) after a verb introduces a description of the action: 他说得很好, 妹妹长得很高, 他跑得比我快. This is different from a result complement such as 做完, and from an adverb before the verb such as 很好地.
The contrast example uses the result complement 完: 他说完了. 得 describes manner or degree; a result complement states the outcome directly.

examples.translation: My younger sister has grown very tall.

lessons.title: Quantity complements: duration and measurement
lessons.summary: Duration follows the verb: 住了两年; measurement follows an adjective: 大两岁.
body: Duration (时量补语) follows the verb, often with 了: 我住了一年, 他等了一个小时. An adjective plus a quantity states a difference or size: 他比我大三岁, 这条路长一百米, 这座山有一千米高.
The contrast example uses 次: 我去过两次北京. 次 counts occasions; duration counts how long, and adjective + quantity measures a difference.

examples.reading: wǒ zài Zhōngguó zhù le liǎng nián.
examples.translation: I lived in China for two years.

examples.reading: tā děng le yí ge xiǎoshí.
tā bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.translation: He is three years older than me.

examples.reading: wǒ qù guo liǎng cì Běijīng.
examples.translation: I have been to Beijing twice.

lessons.title: Subject-predicate predicates
lessons.summary: A whole subject-predicate phrase comments on the topic: 他身体很好.
body: In a 主谓谓语句 the predicate itself is a subject-predicate phrase: 他身体很好 (topic 他, comment 身体很好), 这件事我不清楚. The first noun is the topic, and the following subject belongs to it.
The contrast example uses an ordinary verb-plus-object sentence: 我喜欢汉语. A subject-predicate predicate comments on a topic; an ordinary sentence states an action with an object.

examples.translation: He is in very good health.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì wǒ bù qīngchu.
examples.translation: I am not clear about this matter.

lessons.title: 还是 choice questions
lessons.summary: A还是B? asks the listener to choose one of two options.
body: 还是 makes an alternative question: 你想喝茶还是咖啡？ 今天还是明天？ The answer is one of the two, not yes or no. Do not add 吗 to the sentence.
The contrast example uses 吗: 你想喝茶吗？ 吗 makes a yes-no question; 还是 offers two choices. Choose the particle that matches the answer you expect.

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishì kāfēi?
examples.translation: Would you like tea or coffee?

examples.reading: nǐ zuò huǒchē háishì zuò fēijī?
examples.translation: Will you take the train or the plane?

lessons.title: Imperative sentences with 别
lessons.summary: Commands start with a verb or 请; 别… tells someone not to do it.
body: An imperative drops the subject and starts with the verb, often with 请 (please) or 别 (do not): 请坐, 请喝茶, 别说话. 别 is direct and spoken.
The contrast example uses 不要: 请不要在教室里跑. 别 and 不要 both command someone not to act; 不要 is fuller and more formal, while 别 is short and colloquial.

examples.reading: qǐng búyào zài jiàoshì li pǎo.
examples.translation: Please do not run in the classroom.

lessons.title: 是 for explanation and characteristics
lessons.summary: 是 plus a quality or category explains what something is like: 这个苹果是甜的.
body: 是 can explain a characteristic or category, often with 的 at the end: 这个苹果是甜的, 这件衣服是毛的, 他是教书的. It states a fact about the subject rather than an action.
The contrast example uses 很: 这个苹果很甜. 很 describes the degree; 是…的 affirms the quality as a fact or classification. They are close in meaning but not interchangeable in structure.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu shì máo de.
examples.translation: This garment is made of wool.
He is a teacher by profession.

lessons.title: 有 + quantity: reaching a measure
lessons.summary: 有 plus a quantity says how deep, long or high something is.
body: 有 with a quantity states an extent or measurement: 这条河有十米深, 这条路有二十公里长, 这座山有一千米高. It says the thing reaches that measure.
The contrast example uses 很: 这条河很深. 很 only says the degree (very deep); 有 + quantity gives a measured amount.

examples.reading: zhè tiáo hé yǒu shí mǐ shēn.
examples.translation: This river is ten metres deep.

examples.reading: zhè tiáo lù yǒu èrshí gōnglǐ cháng.
examples.translation: This road is twenty kilometres long.

examples.reading: zhè zuò shān yǒu yì qiān mǐ gāo.
examples.translation: This mountain is one thousand metres high.

lessons.title: Existential sentences: place + verb + 着 + noun
lessons.summary: A place plus a verb with 着 says something is there: 桌子上放着一本书.
body: Place words start the sentence, then a verb with 着, then the thing: 桌子上放着一本书, 墙上挂着一幅画, 门口站着一个人. 着 marks a state, and the thing after it is indefinite, so use 一本 / 一个, not 这 / 那.
The contrast example uses 在: 我在看书. An existential sentence describes what is at a place (a state); 在 + verb describes an action happening now.

examples.reading: zhuōzi shàng fàng zhe yì běn shū.
examples.translation: There is a book on the table.

examples.reading: qiáng shàng guà zhe yì fú huà.
examples.translation: There is a picture on the wall.

examples.reading: ménkǒu zhàn zhe yí ge rén.
examples.translation: A person is standing at the door.

lessons.title: Comparisons: A 比 B …
lessons.summary: 比 compares two things; 没有 says not as … as; with a verb use 得.
pattern: A + 比 + B + adj + 数量; A + 没有 + B + adj
A + 比 + B + V + 得 + adj
body: 比 (bǐ) puts the standard after it: 他比我高, 我比弟弟大两岁. To say A is not as … as B, use 没有: 我没有他高; to say A reaches B, use 有: 他有我这么高. With a verb, add 得: 他比我唱得好.
The contrast example uses 一样: 他和我一样高. 比 shows a difference; 一样 says the two are equal.

examples.reading: wǒ bǐ dìdi dà liǎng suì.
examples.translation: I am two years older than my brother.
He is not as tall as me.
He is as tall as me.

lessons.title: 是……的: emphasizing details of an event
lessons.summary: 是……的 stresses when, where, how or who did something: 我是昨天到的.
body: 是……的 emphasizes a detail of an event, usually in the past: 我是昨天到的, 他是坐火车来的, 我是在书店买的. The 是 can be dropped; the 的 stays. Use it to answer when / where / how questions about the event.
The contrast example uses 了: 我昨天去了北京. 是……的 emphasizes the detail; 了 simply says the action was completed. Both are possible orders with 昨天, so the word-order exercise is skipped for that example.

examples.reading: tā shì zuò huǒchē lái de.
wǒ shì zài shūdiàn mǎi de.
examples.translation: I bought it at the bookshop.

lessons.title: Pivotal sentences: 请 叫 让 someone do something
lessons.summary: 请/叫/让 take a person, and that person does the next verb: 请他来, 让我走.
body: In a pivotal sentence the object of 请 / 叫 / 让 is also the subject of the next verb: 老师请我们回答问题, 妈妈叫我早点睡, 他让我先走. Do not add 是 or 的 between them.
The contrast example uses 和: 我和朋友一起去. 和 joins two people who do one action together; 请 / 叫 / 让 introduce a person who then performs a second action.

examples.translation: The teacher asked us to answer the question.
Mum told me to go to bed early.
I will go together with a friend.

lessons.title: Double objects with 给: send someone something
lessons.summary: S + V + 给 + person + thing: 他寄给我一个包裹.
body: With verbs such as 送, 寄 and 告诉, put 给 before the person: 他送给我一本书, 他寄给我一个包裹, 老师发给我们一张纸. The thing follows the person; 给 marks the receiver.
The contrast example uses 把: 他把书给我. The 把 construction moves the thing before the verb; the 给 double-object sentence keeps person and thing after the verb.

examples.reading: tā jì gěi wǒ yí ge bāoguǒ.
māma jì gěi wǒ yì fēng xìn.
tā sòng gěi wǒ yì zhāng piào.

examples.translation: He gave the book to me.

lessons.title: Alternative complex sentences: 是……，还是……
lessons.summary: (是) A，还是 B offers two clauses as choices.
body: (是)……，还是…… joins two clauses as choices: 你是在家看书，还是去图书馆？ 我们是今天走，还是明天走？ It is the sentence form of the A还是B? question, and the answer is one clause.
The contrast example uses 吗: 你明天走吗？ 吗 asks for yes or no; 是…还是… asks the listener to pick one of two clauses.

examples.text: 你是在家看书，还是去图书馆？
examples.reading: nǐ shì zài jiā kàn shū, háishì qù túshūguǎn?
examples.translation: Will you read at home, or go to the library?

examples.text: 我们是今天走，还是明天走？
examples.reading: wǒmen shì jīntiān zǒu, háishì míngtiān zǒu?
examples.translation: Shall we leave today, or tomorrow?

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng chī mǐfàn, háishì miàntiáo?
examples.translation: Would you like rice, or noodles?

lessons.title: Concessive sentences: 虽然……，但是……
lessons.summary: 虽然 admits a fact, 但是 turns to the opposite result.
body: 虽然 (suīrán) concedes something; 但是 turns to the unexpected: 虽然很贵，但是质量很好; 虽然下雨，我们还是去了. The two clauses often contrast, and 但是 belongs in the second clause.
The contrast example uses 因为…所以…: 因为下雨，所以比赛取消了. 虽然…但是… links concession and turn; 因为…所以… links cause and result.

examples.text: 虽然很贵，但是质量很好。
examples.reading: suīrán hěn guì, dànshì zhìliàng hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: It is expensive, but the quality is good.

examples.text: 虽然下雨，我们还是去了。
examples.reading: suīrán xià yǔ, wǒmen háishì qù le.
examples.translation: Although it rained, we still went.

examples.text: 虽然他很累，但是他还在工作。
examples.reading: suīrán tā hěn lèi, dànshì tā hái zài gōngzuò.
examples.translation: Although he is tired, he is still working.

examples.text: 因为下雨，所以比赛取消了。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
examples.translation: Because it rained, the match was cancelled.

lessons.title: Cause and result: 因为……，所以……
lessons.summary: 因为 gives the reason, 所以 the result.
body: 因为…所以… links a reason and its result: 因为生病，所以他没来; 因为下雪，路上车很少. 因为 can stand alone in an answer, and 所以 usually introduces the second clause.
The contrast example uses 虽然…但是…: 虽然下雨，但是我还是去了. A causal sentence says one thing caused another; a concessive sentence admits a fact and turns against it.

examples.reading: yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ bú qù.
examples.translation: Because it is raining, I am not going.

examples.reading: yīnwèi shēngbìng, tā méi lái shàngkè.
examples.translation: Because he was ill, he did not come to class.

examples.text: 因为下雪，所以路上车很少。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià xuě, suǒyǐ lù shang chē hěn shǎo.
examples.translation: Because it snowed, there were few cars on the road.

examples.text: 虽然下雨，但是我还是去了。
examples.reading: suīrán xià yǔ, dànshì wǒ háishì qù le.
examples.translation: Although it rained, I still went.

lessons.title: 一……就……: as soon as
lessons.summary: 一……就… links two immediate actions: 我一放学就回家。
body: 一……就…… says the second action follows the first immediately: 他一回来就给我打电话; 天一冷就下雪. The two clauses share the subject, and 就 stands in the second.
The contrast example uses 先……再……: 我先吃饭，再去散步. 一…就… stresses that there is no gap; 先…再… only lists steps in order.

examples.reading: wǒ yí fàngxué jiù huí jiā.
examples.translation: As soon as school finishes, I go home.

examples.text: 他一回来就给我打电话。
examples.reading: tā yì huílai jiù gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.translation: As soon as he gets back, he will call me.

examples.reading: tiān yì lěng jiù xià xuě.
examples.translation: As soon as it turns cold, it snows.

examples.reading: wǒ xiān chī fàn, zài qù sàn bù.
examples.translation: I will eat first, then go for a walk.

lessons.title: 持续态: verb + 着
lessons.summary: 着 after a verb says a state continues or an action keeps going.
body: 着 marks a continuing state or action: 门开着, 他坐着看书, 树上挂着很多苹果. It often describes how things are, especially a background scene. Compare the progressive 在, which says an action is happening now.
The contrast example uses 在: 他在看书. 着 presents a held state or continuation; 在 presents an action in progress at this moment.

examples.reading: shù shàng guà zhe hěnduō píngguǒ.
examples.translation: Many apples are hanging on the tree.
The light is on in the room.

lessons.title: 经历态: verb + 过
lessons.summary: 过 says someone has had the experience at least once: 我去过中国。
body: As an aspect, 过 says an action has been experienced, not when it happened: 我去过中国, 他吃过烤鸭. Ask 你吃过…吗？ Negate with 没: 我没去过. It does not combine with a specific past time such as 昨天; use 了 for that.
The contrast example uses 了: 我昨天去了北京. 过 looks back over an indefinite past; 了 anchors the action to the stated occasion.

examples.translation: Have you ever eaten roast duck?
I have never been to Shanghai.

lessons.title: Number + measure: floors, classes, grades
lessons.summary: A number plus a measure names an ordered item: 二楼, 三班, 五年级.
pattern: numeral + measure (+ noun): 二楼, 三班
numeral + 年级 / 层 / 号
body: To name floors, classes, grades and rooms, put the number directly before the measure word, without 第: 二楼, 三班, 五年级, 四号房间. This is a label for an ordered unit, not a count of things: 三楼 means the third floor, not three floors.
The contrast example uses 第: 我的座位在第五排. 第 + number gives the position in a row or sequence; number + measure names a fixed label such as a floor or a class.

examples.translation: My home is on the third floor.

examples.reading: wǒ de zuòwèi zài dì-wǔ pái.
examples.translation: My seat is in the fifth row.

lessons.title: Approximate numbers: 几, 十多, 一年多
lessons.summary: 几 asks a small approximate number; 多 after a number or a measure means more than.
body: 几 (jǐ) asks for a rough small number: 几个人, 几个苹果. 多 after a number means more than: 十多个, 三十多个人. 多 after the measure means more than that many units: 三年多, 五个多月. Do not say 三个多人.
The contrast example uses 多少: 你们班有多少人？ 几 suggests a small amount and needs a measure word; 多少 asks about any amount and goes straight before the noun.

examples.reading: jiàoshì li yǒu shí duō ge xuéshēng.
examples.translation: There are more than ten students in the classroom.

examples.reading: tā xué le yì nián duō Hànyǔ.
examples.translation: He has studied Chinese for more than a year.
How many people are there in your class?
